races.name: Killarney Park 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Balance Of Trade
runners_data.note: Paul Mulligan runner who has been placed once from six hurdle starts at similar trips on good ground; his hold-up style means he'll be shuffled back into the congested rear group where getting a clear run is far from guaranteed, and his flat form at 16f suggests stamina is an asset if he can get first run.|

runners_data.name: Connor Of Mali
runners_data.note: Finished pulled-up last time out and carries a fade-in-finish flag; L J Archdeacon has one placing from two over hurdles in the last 14 days, but this horse is a genuine hold-up type who will need traffic to clear and rivals to stop in front — both uncertain in a slowly-run affair.|

runners_data.name: Delusional
runners_data.note: Peter Maher's runner has shown three placed efforts in flat form on good ground and arrives 25 days fresh; a natural hold-up type shifted into a midfield mapping here because of the crowded rear, and the risk is that a slow gallop renders his finishing effort too late to count.|

runners_data.name: Divelment
runners_data.note: Three places from ten flat starts including a couple on standard going; William Durkan has a 1/3 record over the last 14 days which is an angle worth noting, though 49 days off the track and a deep hold-up style that will be difficult to express in this race shape are clear concerns.|

runners_data.name: Minella Buoy
runners_data.note: John J Nallen's runner has shown little in four flat outings, all on a range of ground, and wearing headgear (hood); has the hold-up flag but no win or place to show for it, and at 46 days since last run confidence in his readiness is limited.|

runners_data.name: Notahairoutofplace
runners_data.note: Fell/unseated last time and pulled up the run before; R K Watson's runner carries a fade-in-finish flag and a concerning recent form string, and the hold-up style means this horse is particularly vulnerable to the slow gallop washing away any chance of a late surge.|

runners_data.name: Private Larry
runners_data.note: The one horse in the field with a hurdles win to his name (12f, good ground), trained by Alan McIntyre who lands 1/1 in the last 14 days; a hold-up type carrying the fade flag, but his previous winning form over a similar trip and going gives him an edge in a race where stamina will be tested.|

runners_data.name: Words Unspoken
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and genuinely unexposed after just one run on the flat (4th over 16f, good); S Curling's in-form yard (1/6 over 14 days) and Phillip Enright in the saddle are positives, and the unknown style tag means the race shape could suit if he settles into a prominent position off the slow pace.|

runners_data.name: Cite Florale
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's gelding, who carries 7lb less than the field, has placed twice from three flat starts including a second at 12f and a third on good ground; a prominent-style runner who is ideally positioned to sit behind Misty Cove and challenge late, and at 52 days absent the fitness question is the only note of caution.|

runners_data.name: Honey Dale
runners_data.note: Paul Mulligan second string (his other runner is Balance Of Trade), who has struggled in flat form — 12th, 12th on good ground — and arrives 25 days fresh; a genuine hold-up type that will likely get stuck in the congested midfield, and the fade-in-finish flag compounds concerns over ability to deliver a winning effort.|

runners_data.name: Misty Cove
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's front-runner won over 10f on soft and placed twice on standard going; 49 days off the track is a question mark, but structurally she holds the best position in this race — unchallenged at the head of affairs, she controls the pace and sets the parameters every other horse must solve.|

runners_data.name: No Bother Aoife
runners_data.note: Second Cromwell runner, which is an angle of interest; she ran only four days ago (a significant flag) and carries the fade-in-finish warning, but her run on good at Killarney (7th in a 12f) and the headgear switch (tongue-tie noted) are worth registering — a hold-up type who will need everything to go right late.|

races.paceDynamic: Misty Cove is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 3-Y-O maiden hurdle over 2m1f at Killarney, and with no other genuine leader to challenge her, she can dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop from the front without ever being seriously pressured. Cite Florale is the only other prominent-profile runner and will track Misty Cove, meaning the pace is likely to be steady rather than searching, which rewards those travelling sweetly in the first half of the race. The field is saturated with hold-up horses — Balance Of Trade, Connor Of Mali, Delusional, Divelment, Honey Dale, No Bother Aoife, Private Larry, Minella Buoy, Notahairoutofplace and Words Unspoken are all rear-to-midfield types — creating a bunched, traffic-sensitive group that will need clear runs and quick acceleration from the final bend. A steady gallop set by an uncontested leader strongly favours a prominent or well-positioned midfield horse that travels into the race rather than a genuine deep-seated hold-up type finishing from last; the tactical verdict is that the horse best able to track Misty Cove and pounce turning for home — essentially a prominent or forward-midfield profile — holds the structural edge. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race map can place honestly at the rear; of the redistibuted runners, Delusional and Divelment have the form profiles most likely to push forward from their natural position, though Misty Cove and Cite Florale remain best placed to actually secure the front two berths.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Misty Cove controls and wins
scenarios.trigger: If Misty Cove dictates a modest gallop unchallenged and the hold-up pack cannot generate the closing burst needed to reel her in from the rear.
scenarios.body: Gavin Cromwell's runner sets her own fractions over the 2m1f trip, and with stamina her likely strong suit on good ground, she can simply outstay a field stuck in traffic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent runner pounces late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough that a hold-up horse tracking in a forward-midfield position picks up the scent of Misty Cove late and storms past on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Cite Florale or Words Unspoken, travelling smoothly behind the leader, gets first run turning for home and the combination of a good jump at the final flight and a sustained gallop sees them cut down the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Steady pace suits late closers
scenarios.trigger: If the held-up horses manage to avoid traffic and find their stride in the straight, taking advantage of a race that has been run at a crawl.
scenarios.body: A slow gallop paradoxically can compress the field enough that a horse like Delusional or Private Larry, getting a clean passage wide, swoops past tiring rivals in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace chaos, outsider benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Divelment or Delusional push forward early and create a faster-than-expected gallop, scrambling the race shape and leaving an unconsidered runner to fill the frame.
scenarios.body: A more searching gallop over 2m1f would expose horses lacking the fitness or jumping experience in this 3-Y-O field, and a lightly-raced type like Words Unspoken travelling well in behind could emerge late.

watchPoints.text: Misty Cove's uncontested lead is the defining factor — if she bowls along at her own pace over 2m1f without any pressure from rivals, she may be very hard to catch from the front.

No Bother Aoife runs just four days after her last start, an unusually quick turnaround for a jumps maiden, and jockeys and punters should watch the paddock and market carefully for signs of anything amiss.

The field is packed with horses carrying a fade-in-finish flag (Connor Of Mali, Honey Dale, No Bother Aoife, Notahairoutofplace, Private Larry) — if the pace is slow and the race develops into a sprint, these horses could all fail to see out the finish together, opening the door for a non-flagged rival.

Words Unspoken is the only runner tagged as genuinely unknown in style with just one career run — if she positions prominently off the slow pace, she becomes a significant unknown quantity for the in-form Curling/Enright combination.
Cite Florale's 7lb weight advantage over most of the field is a structural edge in a race where all horses are OR 120 — in a compressed finish, that allowance could be decisive.

races.name: Killarney Grand Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Fraher Field
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a win on Good at 16f and a placed run at 20f; Phillip Enright partners a horse who jumps reliably and should be bang in contention tracking Torque De Lune, though her form tail-off over longer trips (11th, 7th) bears watching over 2m7f.

runners_data.name: Pets Georgina
runners_data.note: Opened her account over hurdles on Good ground and placed at 24f, making her one of the better-credentialled stayers here; J J Slevin in the saddle for a well-performing trainer unit (T14: 3/16) is a strong angle, and she is likely to be prominent from the start.

runners_data.name: Some Pretender
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins-trained with consistent placed form across varied ground, though she is yet to win over hurdles in five attempts; Brian Hayes's placing will be sharp but this mare's record suggests she finds a way to finish second or third rather than winning.

runners_data.name: Another Blunder
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type with a worrying trend of fading in the finish, and her form reads 6-13-12-10-7 in recent starts on Good — nothing in the record suggests she will reverse that pattern over 2m7f today.

runners_data.name: Chisel Hill
runners_data.note: Placed twice in three hurdle starts, including second over 20f on Good, which makes her one of the more interesting prominent types at a lower OR of 108; first-time-out form here (Sam Ewing, quiet trainer) but the distance form is real.

runners_data.name: Glenmore Graduate
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and flagged for fading in the finish, with just one run on comparable ground; Peter Maher's charge is very much an unknown quantity over this stamina-testing trip and the lack of evidence is a significant concern.

runners_data.name: Jessie Roe
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has finished between 6th and 10th in all seven starts on comparable ground — form is consistently poor, and the tongue-tie has not altered the pattern; very hard to make a case for her in any scenario.

runners_data.name: Keyser Smokesy
runners_data.note: Competes from the rear but the map places him in midfield due to the volume of true hold-up types in this field; his OR of 77 is markedly the lowest in the race, his recent form includes a pulled-up run, and he is essentially racing at a significant class disadvantage here.

runners_data.name: Mysilverriverfeale
runners_data.note: Placed at 22f on Good ground and won over a middle trip — a combination of tongue-tie, hood, and a two-mile-seven trip on Good could suit if she jumps cleanly; Daniel King's mount is an interesting each-way profile if the pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Torque De Lune
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter for John Joseph Hanlon who has a quiet recent record (T14: 0/24), and the STYLE_FIT flag acknowledges she may be ridden more conservatively than usual; she is best treated as a pace influence rather than a winning banker.

runners_data.name: Tumbling In
runners_data.note: Three runs, three placed finishes, all at 16f on Good — the step up to 2m7f is a significant unknown for this lightly raced mare, and whether her consistency will stretch to a staying trip is the key question.

runners_data.name: Uno Me I Like My T
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a chaotic form string of P-F-3-F-P and a tongue-tie; the jumping errors are a serious safety concern over 15 hurdles at Killarney, and her chance depends entirely on getting round cleanly.

runners_data.name: Daily Devotion
runners_data.note: Just two runs under rules with nothing to recommend her on form — 13th and 8th on Good and Soft respectively — and the step up in trip to 2m7f looks ambitious for a lightly raced four-year-old.

runners_data.name: Greenroad Girl
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed with no form data available and going unknown; a total wildcard whose chance rests entirely on raw ability and an uncomplicated round of jumping.

runners_data.name: Sonna Lady
runners_data.note: Two runs, both on Good ground, finishing 7th and 9th — the Hanlon yard also saddles Torque De Lune, and Josh Younge (7) takes a relatively weak book; this mare is lightly raced and unproven but the stable angle is worth noting as a long-shot curiosity.

races.paceDynamic: Torque De Lune is the confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner mares maiden hurdle over 2m7f at Killarney, and with no other genuine leader to press her, she is likely to control a sustainable, measured gallop on good ground — a tempo that keeps the race together rather than stringing it out. Behind her, a cluster of prominent types including Fraher Field, Pets Georgina, Some Pretender, Chisel Hill, and Mysilverriverfeale will contest the early positions, creating a competitive but not frantic early order. This field holds more prominent runners than can all secure their preferred position simultaneously, and among them Fraher Field and Pets Georgina — both with strong Good-ground records and solid form lines — are most likely to actually establish themselves close to Torque De Lune's shoulder. A controlled early pace that gradually quickens into the Killarney straight over this staying trip will reward horses that can travel prominently or in a handy midfield position, track the leader, and sustain their effort over the final two hurdles — this race shape strongly favours prominent and hold-up-to-midfield types with proven stamina on Good ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Torque De Lune Controls Clean
scenarios.trigger: If Torque De Lune sets an uncontested, well-judged pace and the prominent pack settles without early friction.
scenarios.body: Torque De Lune dictates a sustainable gallop that suits her stamina credentials, and horses tracking her closely in the first three have every chance to challenge and overhaul her late; the trip on Good ground favours those who conserve energy in the early stages and produce a clean round of jumping.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Heats It Up
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types refuse to settle and the pace becomes genuinely strong over the first mile.
scenarios.body: A hot pace fragments the field and rewards those who drop back slightly to a true midfield position with a smooth jumping round, while the front-running group tire late on the testing 2m7f trip; Chisel Hill and Mysilverriverfeale, both placed at this distance on Good ground, could be the beneficiaries of an even pace collapse up front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and hold-up horses get a clean passage through to challenge.
scenarios.body: Genuine hold-up types are thin on the ground here since the most notable rear-of-field runners carry form concerns or redistribution caveats, so this scenario is structurally unlikely; however, Tumbling In — consistently placed and lightly raced — could emerge from a patient midfield position if the early movers empty.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Chaos, Rank Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers or a chaotic early order scrambles the race entirely and an unconsidered runner navigates cleanly.
scenarios.body: In a 15-runner field with novice-grade jumping on undulating Killarney terrain, a clean, uncomplicated round of jumping alone could bring a lightly-raced or unproven runner into contention; Sonna Lady or Greenroad Girl, both unexposed, could benefit from sheer fortune if the race falls apart.

watchPoints.text: Torque De Lune's actual tempo is critical — if Harry Sexton (7) allows her to idle in front and the prominent pack closes up, the race becomes a sprint to the last, which will compress the finishing order dramatically.

Uno Me I Like My T has fallen or been pulled up in four of her last five starts — monitor her in the early stages over the first few hurdles as a potential in-running hazard for horses travelling behind her.

The cluster of prominent runners — Fraher Field, Pets Georgina, Some Pretender, and Chisel Hill — all wanting to be in the first three could create early jostling and put some of the smaller-OR horses (Chisel Hill, Mysilverriverfeale) out of their comfort zone before halfway.

Mysilverriverfeale carries both tongue-tie and hood — watch for whether the headgear combination produces a more tractable or a more free-going early display, as it materially affects how the midfield shapes up behind the leaders.

Going is listed as unknown at Killarney for all races — any last-minute ground update closer to post time could significantly alter the going suitability ratings, particularly for runners with form specifically on Good ground.

races.name: Lee Strand Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Pray Tell
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field; Paddy Cleary takes 7lb off but this is a 10-year-old carrying 166lbs on a 63-day break — stamina reserves are the key question if the gallop is genuine throughout.
runners_data.comment: Pray Tell was fourth last time out and has raced over today's trip before, with a second among his last five starts standing out. Yet to win in that spell and shouldering 166 lb, the 63-day layoff since is the main concern for this leading contender.

runners_data.name: Idy Wood
runners_data.note: Keith Donoghue takes the ride for in-form Gavin Cromwell (2/45 last 14 days); hold-up style suits this scenario ideally, has winning form on good ground over similar trips, but 93 days off warrants monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Idy Wood struck form with a win in this sequence and rates 127 for us, third best in the field. He was pulled up last time out after a 93-day gap, but the deeper figures and profile make him the narrow selection here.

runners_data.name: Magnor Glory
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type who handles good going with 15/15 sim-going runs to his name; 5-pound claimer Alan O'Sullivan lightens the load but the horse's OR 125 suggests he needs to find improvement against this field.
runners_data.comment: Magnor Glory heads our figures at 129, clear of his official mark, with two thirds among his last five starts. Fourth last time out having been pulled up before that, he's winless in that spell but the placed efforts make him the leading threat here.

runners_data.name: Jacovec Cavern
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on good ground and placed at 22f — the trip is within range; headgear listed as 'p' (probably hood or cheekpieces) and a 5lb claim from Richard Condon helps; 32-day turnaround is fine.
runners_data.comment: Jacovec Cavern was third last time out and second before that, having won earlier in this sequence, though two unplaced efforts further back show inconsistency. He's fit from a recent run and has raced over today's trip before, which both count in his favour.

runners_data.name: Thornleigh Frank
runners_data.note: Won over 22f on good ground and has placed consistently from a prominent position; headgear noted, and the 53-day break is acceptable — ran third at 22f on good ground last time, which is encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Thornleigh Frank was third last time out but that followed two ninths and a sixth in his previous three starts — a mixed level of form. Winless in that spell, he does have today's trip covered and carries a fair weight, without standing out from this field.

runners_data.name: Nas Na Riogh
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead yard in form (4/35 last 14 days); Darragh O'Keeffe is a strong hold-up jockey; blinkered hold-up type whose recent form reads poorly but the stable form lifts interest considerably.
runners_data.comment: Nas Na Riogh was unplaced last time out, continuing a modest sequence of sixths and a fourth through his last five starts without a win. He has raced over today's trip before and carries a workable weight, but the form offers little to suggest an upturn is imminent.

runners_data.name: Nytol
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a modest recent record — unseated last time and has struggled to complete or place in his last several starts; Terence O'Brien has not been firing recently with this horse, and the 57-day break is neutral.
runners_data.comment: Nytol was unseated last time out, with two sevenths and a pulled-up effort further back in a winless sequence. She rates below her official mark for us, though today's trip is nothing new to her — the form offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Frankendael
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type whose best effort of 3rd came over 16f on good ground — the step up to 2m7f is a significant distance question; only two placed runs from 10 starts, but the style is right for the shape.
runners_data.comment: Frankendael is rated above his official mark for us, with a third among his last four starts standing out. Sixth last time out and yet to win in that sequence, the concern is consistency — but on his better efforts he's up with the leading dangers here.

runners_data.name: Cobra Queen
runners_data.note: Won twice at OR level on good ground and has strong prominent form over staying trips; 7-year-old mare who drops in trip slightly from last run, but 13/15 sim-going record is outstanding and she has strong credentials here.
runners_data.comment: Cobra Queen won twice earlier in this sequence but her last two starts read pulled up and eighth, a clear dip in form. She rates above her official mark for us and has raced over today's trip before, though the recent puzzling efforts are the query.

runners_data.name: My Gaffer
runners_data.note: Won over 23f on good ground last time out for John Patrick Ryan, who has been notably active (3/16 last 14 days); hold-up style is a genuine asset in this race shape and 13/15 on similar going underlines suitability.
runners_data.comment: My Gaffer was fourth last time out, having won the run before that, with a seventh, eighth and unplaced effort further back in this sequence. He rates above his official mark for us and has raced over today's trip before, form that leaves him with claims in this field.

runners_data.name: Warriors Wood
runners_data.note: Young 6-year-old improver with three wins from 11 starts on good ground; placed at 20f, 20f, and 22f in recent runs showing he handles the trip — Brian Hayes is a strong booking and he could yet break into the first three.
runners_data.comment: Warriors Wood was third last time out, but had won the run before that, adding a second and only an unseated effort figuring among his last five starts. He rates well above his official mark for us and returns having last run just a month ago.

runners_data.name: Elusive Ogie
runners_data.note: In-form prominent racer who has shown ability at this level; though naturally a front-runner, the overcrowded pace scenario means he is pushed back into midfield against his preferred style — his chance depends on finding cleaner air than the map suggests he'll get.
runners_data.comment: Elusive Ogie was unplaced last time out, and fell the run before that, with a ninth, fifth and third further back in a mixed sequence. Yet to win in that spell, he rates in line with his official mark for us, leaving him with more questions than claims.

runners_data.name: Kamino Bello
runners_data.note: Ran just 1 day ago, which is extremely unusual — connections will need a compelling reason for this quick turnaround; hold-up style in an already hold-up heavy field, and recent form figures of 560-60 don't inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Kamino Bello was unplaced last time out, continuing a modest sequence that includes two sixths and a fifth without a win. He rates below his official mark for us and the yard is out of form, though a quick reappearance just a day on is one plus.

runners_data.name: Moon Mission
runners_data.note: Five-year-old improver who won over 18f on good ground — useful profile; front-running instincts are genuine but with so many prominent horses in this field, he is likely to be pushed further back than ideal, which blunts his chance.
runners_data.comment: Moon Mission was fifth last time out, having won the run before that, with an unplaced effort before it, and a third and fourth further back. He rates well below his official mark for us, leaving him hard to fancy on current figures despite that win in the mix.

runners_data.name: Has Me Dreaming
runners_data.note: Returned from a 681-day absence last time, finishing third on good ground over 16f — this is his second run back and the step up to 2m7f is a big ask; his natural prominence will be hard to assert in such a crowded early pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Has Me Dreaming won last time out, but that was 681 days ago with only a third to precede it — a lightly raced profile. He rates well below his official mark for us, and such a lengthy absence makes him hard to trust fully in this field.

runners_data.name: Hees Dynamite
runners_data.note: Four wins in similar conditions and a strong staying profile over heavy distances; off 200 days and returning to a competitive handicap — prominent by nature but likely to find himself further back than ideal given the pace volume in this field.
runners_data.comment: Hees Dynamite was pulled up last time out, though three wins feature among his last five starts including twice in succession before that letdown. A 200-day absence and bottom spot on our figures make him hard to fancy, even with today's trip previously covered.

runners_data.name: Burru
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on good ground most recently and has consistent placed form on similar going (15/15); a true prominent racer who will find it difficult to get his natural position, but if he manages to slot in close enough he cannot be dismissed.
runners_data.comment: Burru was unplaced last time out, having won the run before that, with a pulled-up effort, an eighth and a third further back. He rates close to his official mark for us and has raced over today's trip before, but the formline is too patchy for real confidence.

runners_data.name: Woodstream Lad
runners_data.note: Consistent placer on good ground (15/15 sim-going) who has finished second and third recently; like several others, a naturally prominent horse who faces the frustration of a field where prominent berths are at a premium — form solid but the tactical disadvantage is real.
runners_data.comment: Woodstream Lad was fifth last time out but had finished runner-up the run before that, with two pulled-up efforts and a third further back in a stop-start sequence. Yet to win in that run, he rates close to his official mark for us, leaving him hard to trust in this company.

races.paceDynamic: Pray Tell is the one confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to press hard from the outset, should be able to control the tempo from the front over 2m7f on good ground. Magnor Glory, Jacovec Cavern, Thornleigh Frank, Cobra Queen, and Warriors Wood are all natural prominent types who will compete for the early positions just behind, creating a busy but not truly contested lead — the pace is likely to be honest rather than punishing. The field is significantly overloaded with front-running and prominent types: Moon Mission, Elusive Ogie, Has Me Dreaming, Hees Dynamite, Burru, and Woodstream Lad are all genuine prominent horses who cannot all get their natural position, meaning several will be shuffled back into unfamiliar midfield territory against their will. With one controlled pace-setter and a sustained gallop over a staying trip, this race shape most favours hold-up or late-finishing types who can exploit a genuine end-to-end gallop — horses like Idy Wood, Nas Na Riogh, My Gaffer, and Frankendael who are comfortable travelling in behind and picking up ground in the closing stages stand to benefit most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pray Tell Controls, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Pray Tell sets a sustainable pace unchallenged and the race develops into a true staying test in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Pray Tell dictates from the front at a controlled but genuine clip over 2m7f, and as the field thins out on the run-in, the hold-up horses who have been travelling sweetly in behind unleash their finishing runs; the long trip exposes those who have used energy fighting for prominent positions early. Hold-up types with proven form on good ground at staying distances are perfectly suited to this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If several prominent horses manage to wrestle near-front positions early and the pace quickens significantly from halfway, leaving hold-up horses too much to do.
scenarios.body: The pack behind Pray Tell surges forward, creating a strong gallop that paradoxically suits those who can travel prominently at a good clip — Warriors Wood, Cobra Queen, and Jacovec Cavern are genuine form horses for this trip on good ground. Those who secure a position just off the pace and jump fluently throughout will be best placed when the race heats up after the third-last flight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Surprise Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of prominent types cause significant early scrimmaging, disrupting rhythm for multiple fancied runners and creating a stop-start pace.
scenarios.body: Horses redistributed to midfield against their will lose their rhythm in the early stages, burning energy re-establishing position, and those who adapt best to the chaos or are least bothered by it emerge fresh in the straight. Moon Mission, a young improver, and Burru, who won last time out, are among those whose natural prominent style could still get them into contention if they find a clear run late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Converts
scenarios.trigger: If Pray Tell is given a completely unchallenged lead with a very slow early tempo that allows it to conserve enough energy to hold on up the run-in.
scenarios.body: A truly uncontested, pedestrian early pace lulls the field into a false rhythm, and Pray Tell — already OR 128 and the class act at the front — simply never gets headed, as chasers fail to close the gap in time over the testing 2m7f trip. This is the least likely scenario given the competitive nature of the handicap and the number of prominent horses who will ensure at least a respectable gallop.

watchPoints.text: Watch Kamino Bello's fitness and wellbeing closely — running just one day after its last start is highly unusual for a jumper and connections should be quizzed; if the horse shows any signs of distress in the parade ring, this is a major concern for the integrity of the result.

Warriors Wood and Cobra Queen both have strong recent form and will aggressively contest the prominent positions behind Pray Tell — if either secures a clean jumping run from the front rank, they could prove very hard to peg back in the straight.

The cluster of redistributed prominent horses — Moon Mission, Hees Dynamite, Burru, and Woodstream Lad — will create early crowding and scrimmaging; watch for any horse losing its position or being carried wide at the first few flights, as this could destroy their chance before the race has begun.

Idy Wood has been off 93 days for a stable that has been placing horses well (Cromwell 2/45); watch for any market support in the final minutes before the off, as this could be a well-prepared return from a trainer with a strong record with returning horses.

Pray Tell's rider Paddy Cleary claims 7lbs but has limited experience in competitive handicaps at this level — watch whether the horse is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable clip or if Cleary gives it too easy a time in front, which would dramatically increase the chance of a hold-up horse sweeping past in the final two flights.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Daily Money Back Meeting Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Special Cadeau
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner, he will set the tempo from the off; his OR of 138 gives him a class edge but his form string (52360-) suggests he's been out of sorts and 128 days off the track is a notable query at age 8.
runners_data.comment: A couple of placed efforts in his last five starts show he stays competitive, and today's trip is already firmly in his form book. He also tops our figures at 139, though a 128-day absence following a below-par run last time out is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Jasko Des Dames
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's second string with Darragh O'Keeffe up, his two placings at this trip on good going are relevant, though all five recent runs in the dataset were on softer ground which may make him slightly less potent on today's quicker surface.
runners_data.comment: A pair of runner-up efforts underline his ability, even with the placings drifting more recently, and today's trip holds no fears. Fresh after a 99-day break, he rates second on our figures at 135 and remains open to more on this profile.

runners_data.name: The Banger Doyle
runners_data.note: The veteran 10-year-old has solid good-ground form (two top-3 finishes at 16f) but his recent form reads 8660-7 and he has never won in these recent runs — prominent style suits the map position but winning potential looks limited.
runners_data.comment: A swift reappearance within ten days and proven form over today's trip give him claims, and he sits third in our figures at 132, a shade above his current mark. The concern is a sequence yet to feature a top-three finish.

runners_data.name: Drumgill
runners_data.note: Ran just seven days ago and carries the fatigue risk of a quick turnaround; his best sim-going figures are modest and his form string features two pulled-up/unseated entries, making him an unreliable component of any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time having also unseated earlier in this sequence, and the finishing positions elsewhere read no better than midfield. A quick reappearance after just seven days at least points to fitness, with today's trip already covered, but the sequence overall offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Dreal Deal
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old with genuine front-running instincts who finds himself displaced into midfield by the race's traffic — his best recent effort was a runner-up on good going at 20f but racing out of his natural role at this age blunts his chances considerably.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, a big improvement on the modest efforts before it, and he arrives with today's trip already in the book. Fourth in our figures at 131, the 53-day break since is the main query for this leading fancy.

runners_data.name: Gaelic Arc
runners_data.note: A confirmed hold-up horse with the most relevant recent profile: won at 16f on good going, placed at 20f on good, and has genuine tactical pace to arrive late — Harry Sexton's 7lb claim helps with the burden and this is one of the most shape-aligned runners in the field.
runners_data.comment: A useful renewal of form, following a win two starts back, and a runner-up effort last time out, after a rough patch that included a fall. Sixth in our figures at 128 with today's trip proven, the placings alone claim plenty of respect.

runners_data.name: No Flies On Him
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the ride, which is an obvious eyecatcher, and his placed effort at 18f on similar going is a quiet flag; a genuine hold-up type who will benefit if the pace is honest, though his last three runs include two pulled-up efforts which demand respect as a risk factor.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time, following the same fate three starts back, with only a runner-up effort two starts back to offer encouragement. Seventh in our figures at 127, the stop-start profile before that makes him hard to trust fully here.

runners_data.name: Femme Magnifique
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on good ground make her form the most current in the race, but she is a natural front-runner squeezed into a midfield berth by the congestion of prominent types — her chance depends substantially on whether she can recreate her natural rhythm despite the compromised position.
runners_data.comment: Placed in each of her last two starts, including a win two starts back, so the placings read well. She's fresh off a quick 17-day turnaround with today's trip proven, but only eighth in our figures at 116, some way behind the pace there.

runners_data.name: Mic Drop
runners_data.note: Two consecutive wins at 16f and 18f on good ground give him strong current form, and he is lightly raced at 7 — but like Femme Magnifique his front-running instincts are being suppressed by the race shape, and Michael Kenneally's 5lb claim only partially offsets the positional disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins stand out in this profile, a big turnaround after a mixed run of finishes before that. He's fresh off a 17-day gap with today's trip covered, yet only ninth in our figures at 109, marginally below his current mark.

races.paceDynamic: Special Cadeau is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m1f trip on good ground. The field holds more prominent-types than the race shape can absorb — Dreal Deal, Femme Magnifique, and Mic Drop are all natural front-runners or prominent racers who will be squeezed back into midfield roles they do not naturally suit, likely creating minor early crowding before settling behind Special Cadeau and Jasko Des Dames. The Banger Doyle and Drumgill will fill out the prominent positions, leaving Gaelic Arc and No Flies On Him to track from further back as genuine hold-up horses. With one steady pace-setter and no pressure expected up front, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a powerful late run — Gaelic Arc and No Flies On Him are in the best position to exploit a gallop that is likely to be honest but unhurried, with the race decided from the second-last fence onwards.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cadeau Controls, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Special Cadeau sets a measured, uncontested gallop and the race is truly run to suit hold-up horses coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Special Cadeau rolls along at his own pace with Jasko Des Dames and The Banger Doyle in close attendance, compressing the field and setting up a straight-line duel from the last two fences where fresh legs tell. Gaelic Arc and No Flies On Him, genuine hold-up horses with solid good-ground form, arrive on the bridle to pick off the tiring leaders — Gaelic Arc's recent win at 16f on good and No Flies On Him's placed efforts suit this shape precisely.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Special Cadeau dictates at a strong enough clip to deny the hold-up horses and jumps well enough to maintain a decisive advantage approaching the last.
scenarios.body: With no horse able or willing to pressure Special Cadeau early, he gets a soft lead and conserves enough energy to fend off all challengers, particularly if his jumping is fluent through the final circuit. His OR of 138 gives him class to match and his good-ground form (placed at this trip on similar going) backs up this outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Jasko Des Dames or The Banger Doyle press hard enough to turn this into a stamina test that eliminates the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected pace develops as the prominent pack jostles for position, exhausting the hold-up horses' advantage and reducing the race to a war of attrition between the front pair. Jasko Des Dames, with strong form on good ground at this trip and a competent jockey in Darragh O'Keeffe, is best placed of the prominent brigade to grind out the finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Horse Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If one of Dreal Deal, Femme Magnifique, or Mic Drop manages to secure a better-than-expected position and the race unfolds to suit a mid-prominent type.
scenarios.body: Despite being natural front-runners shuffled into midfield roles, any of these three could benefit if the pace quickens irregularly and they are able to travel just behind the leaders in their natural rhythm. Femme Magnifique is in best current form (back-to-back wins, OR 112) and Mic Drop is similar (two consecutive wins), though both carry the significant style-fit discount that makes this the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: Gaelic Arc is the horse most in harmony with the projected race shape — watch whether Harry Sexton settles him cleanly in the early stages, as any trouble finding cover could compromise his late run entirely.

No Flies On Him's pulled-up efforts (last run and two from five) must not be ignored despite the Cobden booking — watch his jumping early as any errors could unsettle his rhythm and end his race before the finish.

Femme Magnifique and Mic Drop are both natural front-runners in suppressed positions; watch the first two furlongs for any scramble as they attempt to push forward — interference to other runners is a real risk.

Special Cadeau has not run for 128 days and is stepping back from 18f to 17f — watch his jumping at the early fences as ring-rust could cost him the clean lead he needs to make his front-running role effective.

Drumgill runs for the second time in eight days — watch his jumping quality in the back straight as stamina reserves may be depleted and errors under fatigue are a meaningful concern in a field of this size.

races.name: Lee Strand Novice Steeplechase (Div I)

runners_data.name: Endless Talking
runners_data.note: Back-to-back winners on Good at Galway and Gowran (16-19f) suggest she's in form and handles this surface well, but as a natural prominent type squeezed into midfield by a congested pace map, she'll need an early resolution of traffic to get anywhere near her favoured position; style-fit discount applies.

runners_data.name: Net Boy
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has won on Good ground over 16-18f, travelling prominent in all his best efforts — with Mark Walsh in the saddle and the benefit of a genuine prominent slot behind Shadow Paddy, he is one of the few horses whose race shape aligns perfectly with his natural style.

runners_data.name: Shadow Paddy
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner who has won four of his last five starts, with five wins and five places on similar Going — he'll take them along from the front at Killarney and sets the entire tempo for this race; STYLE_FIT flag suggests he is racing slightly out of his most comfortable role but his recent record makes him dangerous regardless.

runners_data.name: Cappa Hill
runners_data.note: Won twice on Good ground (16-17f) earlier in his career but has run poorly in his last three starts (1188-7); a natural prominent racer pushed into the midfield pack by the sheer volume of pace types in this field, which compounds his recent form concerns.

runners_data.name: Fast Felix
runners_data.note: Consistent placed record across 14-15 similar-going runs but only two wins suggest he lacks the finishing punch to challenge at this level; a natural prominent type who has held that position in past races, he is one of the horses most likely to actually secure midfield-to-prominent ground here given the redistribution.

runners_data.name: Piccolo Player
runners_data.note: Youngest in the field at OR 104 — lowest-rated runner here — and has not won in six attempts, finishing 2nd once; a natural prominent racer redistributed to midfield because of pace congestion, and the STYLE_FIT discount plus raw class deficit makes his chances slim even in a favourable shape.

runners_data.name: Wing Back
runners_data.note: The only hold-up horse in the field but flagged as a fader in the finish — ran 9th last time and has only one win from 12 similar-going starts; a controlled, front-run pace from Shadow Paddy is precisely the scenario that makes life hardest for a hold-up type, let alone one with a fading profile.

races.paceDynamic: Shadow Paddy is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger pressing from the outside, is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m1f trip at Killarney. Endless Talking, Cappa Hill, and Piccolo Player are all natural prominent racers who will want to travel close to the pace but cannot all occupy that ground — Net Boy and Fast Felix are the most likely to secure the positions immediately behind Shadow Paddy, with the redistributed trio shuffled wider or further back than they would naturally prefer. Wing Back is the lone hold-up type but carries a fading-finish flag and is unlikely to benefit from a race run at this controlled tempo. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the shape can accommodate — Endless Talking, Cappa Hill, and Piccolo Player are all genuine pace horses forced into midfield roles by the cluster, making life harder for each of them. This race shape overwhelmingly favours a horse travelling prominently in a genuine position — Net Boy and Shadow Paddy, sitting exactly where they want to be — while the redistributed types face an uphill task racing out of their natural role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shadow Paddy Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Paddy leads uncontested and the pace remains honest but measured throughout.
scenarios.body: Shadow Paddy dictates from the front without any serious challenger, jumping cleanly and controlling the tempo to suit a front-runner's finish; horses behind face a deteriorating problem as the race develops with no injection of pace to close the gap. Net Boy, travelling closest in a genuine prominent berth, is ideally placed to challenge if Shadow Paddy falters at the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Picks Up
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Paddy is headed or makes a jumping error mid-race, allowing a prominent horse to surge.
scenarios.body: Net Boy or Endless Talking, travelling in the slipstream of the leader, capitalise immediately on any mistake or loss of momentum from Shadow Paddy and drive clear from the second-last; this shape suits horses who have been patient yet prominent, able to quicken off a steady gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Type Breaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early scramble for position resolves quickly and one of Cappa Hill, Endless Talking, or Piccolo Player earns a prominent berth despite the crowded pace map.
scenarios.body: Endless Talking, rated highest among the redistributed trio on recent form (back-to-back wins, 843-11), is best placed to recover ground if she gets a clear run approaching the home turn; the style-fit discount is real, but her form credentials make her the most dangerous of the reshuffled group if the race develops any gaps.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically in the final half-mile and a strong closing run becomes possible.
scenarios.body: Wing Back, the only genuine hold-up type in the field, would need a strong pace to have run into the ground ahead of her and is hampered further by a stamped fading-finish warning; even in a true staying test over this trip at Killarney, the combination of form concerns and running style makes this the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Shadow Paddy's jumping must be monitored — if he makes a significant error at any of the early fences, Net Boy and Endless Talking are immediately poised to inherit the lead with a full stamina reserve.

Endless Talking, Cappa Hill, and Piccolo Player will all jostle for limited prominent ground in the opening half-mile; watch for traffic interference or shuffling back that could leave any of them trapped wide or flat-footed into the first bend.

Wing Back has run just 14 days ago and carries a fading-finish flag — if the pace eases at all in the straight, watch for her to drop out quickly rather than produce the sustained late run her hold-up style needs.

Net Boy's hood usage is worth tracking at the start — if he breaks cleanly and settles behind Shadow Paddy without incident, his position for the race is near-ideal and he becomes the primary danger to the leader at the final fence.

races.name: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Steeplechase (Div I)

runners_data.name: Tippin And Tappin
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner who can dictate from the front in a 18-runner field; recent win at 22f on Good ground is directly relevant, and the 65-day absence is not a major concern given the trainer's 2/7 14-day record suggesting horses arrive fit; likely to control the tempo throughout at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Three straight wins came before a flat eighth last time out, and this gelding has form over today's trip. A 65-day break and a bit of weight to carry leave him needing to rediscover that spark, sitting mid-pack on our figures.

runners_data.name: The Dara Man
runners_data.note: Veteran 11-year-old hold-up type whose best Going form (0W2P in 11 runs on Good) is modest; trainer John Patrick Ryan has been active (3/16 in 14 days) but this horse's tendency to come from well off the pace will be tested in a big, congested field at 2m7f.
runners_data.comment: Top of our figures by a clear margin, with a much-improved third last time out after two pulled-up efforts. Winless in this sequence but fresh from a 47-day break, the form makes this gelding the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Lecale's Diamond
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 24f on Good going, which is the most directly relevant piece of form in the race; hold-up style from Gavin Cromwell, who is a quality handler, and a 51-day break after a win is not unusual — the concern is whether Keith Donoghue can find a clear run in an 18-runner handicap chase.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out after a string of moderate efforts, and already has form over today's distance. Ranked mid-pack on our figures, a 51-day gap since that win adds a slight fitness question.

runners_data.name: Following Orders
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a consistent record on Good ground (10 runs, 0W4P in similar conditions) who should sit just behind the leader and be on the premises throughout; has not won on Good going despite the strong hit-rate, which is a limiting factor, but the 32-day return is fresh enough.
runners_data.comment: A second earlier in this sequence shows the engine is there, though placings have since tailed off to a pulled-up effort and a well-below-par ninth last time out. Still, rank two on our figures keeps this gelding squarely in the picture.

runners_data.name: Jouster
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has been placed in his last four starts (three seconds/thirds/fourths in a row), suggesting consistent form without finding the front; recent 17-day turnaround is quick but not unusual, and the mix of Good and Soft-going form suggests versatility at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without a win in this sequence, finishing no worse than fifth in the last four starts, with form already banked over today's trip. Race-fit off a 17-day turnaround, he sits sixth of eighteen on our figures and can go close again.

runners_data.name: Tropical Image
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 19f on Good and has placed at this course configuration; the 7lb claim for Thomas O'Connor (7) is a useful weight relief, but 12 runs from 15 on similar going without a win in similar conditions is a concern despite the placings.
runners_data.comment: A promising second last time out - her best effort in a run that also included two sixths, a seventh and a pulled-up run - and she already holds form over today's trip. Ranked just outside mid-table on our figures, 46 days off is the one query.

runners_data.name: Made U Look
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose best form is on Soft/Heavy (0W0P on Good in 2 runs) — the Good going here is a genuine concern; won a 25f Heavy-ground chase, so the trip is fine, but the surface switch and the naturally rear-positioned style in a big field both count against.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed sort who won one start back before an unplaced effort last time out, with minor placings either side. Freshened up by a 39-day break, there should be more to find as this profile develops - happy to take on trust rather than hard evidence.

runners_data.name: Kilashee
runners_data.note: Veteran 11-year-old who won over 22f on Good and has shown decent form in those conditions historically; the P last time out on Soft is somewhat excusable given the surface, and John Patrick Ryan's yard is in form (3/16 T14), giving this horse some live claims at a big price.
runners_data.comment: A win at the start of this sequence has been followed by modest placings and a pulled-up effort last time out. She holds form over today's trip and sits mid-pack on our figures, but needs to rediscover that early spark to feature.

runners_data.name: Malton Groove
runners_data.note: Consistent on Good ground with two placings from 12 relevant runs; travels as a true hold-up type but the congestion in this 18-runner field means he will likely end up in midfield rather than his preferred position off the back, and that redistribution tempers his chance in a scenario that depends on a genuine closing run.
runners_data.comment: Rated inside the leading handful here, with a third last time out backing up a good second before that. Two pulled-up efforts further back are a slight concern, but a quick 17-day turnaround and form over today's trip both work in this gelding's favour.

runners_data.name: Early Arrival
runners_data.note: Long-absent (329 days) prominent racer with a strong record in terms of placings at this trip on Good ground (1W6P in 10 similar-going runs); the return from a near 11-month absence is the obvious question mark, but James Barcoe has runners fresh occasionally and the form profile over 2m7f is solid.
runners_data.comment: A good second last time out was the highlight of a mixed campaign, and he already holds form over today's trip. A 329-day absence is the obvious concern, but rank three of eighteen on our figures keeps him in the reckoning.

runners_data.name: Love Like This
runners_data.note: Won over 24f on Good ground at the last relevant run and is in very recent form (7 days ago), suggesting the trainer is keeping this horse sharp; the prominent style at 24f+ is a good fit for this trip, and the combination of recent form, course-appropriate distance, and Good-going record makes this one of the more interesting profiles.
runners_data.comment: A win before a fair fourth last time out - run just seven days ago - continues a consistent sequence with only one finish outside the first five in six starts. She already holds form over today's trip and looks capable of more than her mid-table rating suggests.

runners_data.name: Three County Star
runners_data.note: Five-year-old whose redistribution reflects a genuine hold-up profile forced into midfield by the pack — furthermore flagged as a runner who fades in the finish, which is a serious concern at 2m7f in a big field; 0W0P on similar going in 7 runs and finishing tendency both count against.
runners_data.comment: A moderate sequence of finishes, headed by a sixth last time out, leaves this gelding winless so far. He already holds form over today's trip and a 32-day gap has him fresh, but tenth of eighteen on our figures says he faces a stiff task to figure.

runners_data.name: Fr Gilligansvoyge
runners_data.note: Veteran 13-year-old prominent racer who is remarkably consistent on Good going (1W4P in 14 of 15 applicable runs) at trips including 22-24f; at OR 75 carrying 143lbs, the weight is relatively light, and the 14-day return is sharp without being a red flag given the trainer's moderate record.
runners_data.comment: A win before last time out's third continues a fair run of form that also includes a second, and he already holds form over today's trip. Rated near the bottom of the field on our figures, though, he needs a career-best to trouble these.

runners_data.name: Annie Questions
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in the finish, which is a critical concern at 2m7f; her true hold-up style is further displaced in a crowded rear, and 0W1P across 10 runs on similar going confirms a limited winning profile — the redistribution and finishing pattern together make this a horse to dismiss.
runners_data.comment: A win in the middle of this sequence shows she has it in her, but modest placings either side - including an unplaced effort last time out - look more typical. She holds form over today's trip, though rank 14 of 18 on our figures leaves plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Eddies Pride
runners_data.note: Veteran 12-year-old who is 0W0P on Good going across 7 runs and whose true hold-up style will be compressed into midfield in this large field; the combination of age, poor Good-going record, and positional challenge makes this a very difficult winning case.
runners_data.comment: A sequence of two pulled-up efforts and two unplaced runs, broken only by a fifth, leaves little to recommend her, and last time out was another blank. She already holds form over today's trip, but rank 16 of 18 on our figures makes her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Ladies Well
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who ran second over 24f on Good ground recently and is an interesting proposition at OR 81; the Reserve 1 jockey booking is a minor unknown, and the U (unseated) last time out needs context, but the previous second at this trip and going profile is directly relevant form.
runners_data.comment: Unseated last time out having been a promising second before that, with an eighth, an unplaced effort and a sixth further back. She already holds form over today's trip, but rank 15 of 18 on our figures suggests that placing was the exception.

runners_data.name: Mobile Mamma
runners_data.note: Won over 24f on Good ground and has placed on similar surfaces, showing a genuine affinity for the trip and conditions; however, the 98-day absence and hold-up style redirected into midfield in a big field are the limiting factors — a natural rear-runner who will not get that position today.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back, then fifth, and a fair third last time out. She has form over today's trip, but a 98-day absence and a rank of 13 of 18 on our figures make her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Johnny M
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher in the 7-14 range across all recent runs, flagged as fading in the finish, and carrying a Reserve 3 jockey booking; true hold-up style displaced into midfield and a finishing tendency that works against him at this trip — the form figures confirm this is a horse who competes without threatening.
runners_data.comment: Four unplaced efforts and a seventh make for a blank sequence on bare form, though this gelding is rated a surprising seventh of eighteen on our figures. A 38-day gap since that last run offers a reset, but the bare results give little encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Tippin And Tappin is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner handicap chase over 2m7f, and with no genuine challenger likely to push them from the front, they can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from flag to finish — a significant positional advantage in a race this size. Following Orders, Tropical Image, Love Like This, Fr Gilligansvoyge, Early Arrival, and Ladies Well are all prominent-style types who will compete for the ground just behind the leader, meaning the early-to-middle portion of the race will not be devoid of pace, but the front will remain largely uncontested. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the race map can honestly place at the rear — Malton Groove, Mobile Mamma, Three County Star, Annie Questions, Eddies Pride, and Johnny M are all genuine closers who will in reality be shuffled into midfield rather than enjoying a true hold-up position, compressing the back half of the field and limiting their ability to produce a sustained late run. This race shape — a lone leader setting an honest but unforced tempo with a competitive pack of prominent horses tracking — strongly favours resolute prominent-to-lead types who can travel fluidly in the first three and kick on from the second-last, rather than true closers who will struggle to find daylight in a big, congested field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Dictates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Tippin And Tappin sets an uncontested, well-judged pace and the prominent pack cannot mount a sustained challenge from two out.
scenarios.body: Tippin And Tappin controls every inch of the race from a handy pitch, with the chasing pack burning energy to close a gap that never fully materialises; the 2m7f trip on Good ground suits a relaxed front-runner who can measure their fences without pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the tracking prominent horses travels powerfully throughout and delivers a clean jump at the last to collar the leader.
scenarios.body: The steady early tempo suits a horse who can travel on the bridle in second or third for the bulk of the trip before asserting from the final fence; the trip and going both reward a horse with a high cruising speed rather than a finisher's kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough mid-race to string the field out and create a clear late-running lane.
scenarios.body: A true hold-up type gets a genuine target to aim at and finds daylight in the closing stages, but this scenario is limited in likelihood because the redistributed hold-up horses are unlikely to get their natural position in this congested 18-runner field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Thins The Field
scenarios.trigger: If multiple jumping errors, fallers, or a dramatic pace collapse scramble the race, gifting the winner an uncontested run to the line.
scenarios.body: A big field over fences on a flat pace always carries the risk of one incident reshaping the race entirely; a horse sitting patiently just off the pace in a safe position would be best placed to capitalise if the principals fall away.

watchPoints.text: Tippin And Tappin sets the pace alone — watch whether the prominent pack (Following Orders, Love Like This) applies any pressure from the third fence, as even mild crowding behind the leader could unsettle an otherwise controlled tempo.

Love Like This ran just 7 days ago and arrives very fresh in the market — watch the opening show for any significant market support, as a horse in current form at this trip and going who suits a prominent position is a live runner.

Early Arrival returns from 329 days off the track — watch the paddock and early jumping for any sign of ring-rustiness, as a horse at this level can strip fit or flat depending on how the yard has prepared them.

Lecale's Diamond, Malton Groove, and Mobile Mamma are all genuine hold-up types compressed into a congested midfield — watch the running order at halfway, because if these horses are trapped wide or without cover, their chance evaporates entirely regardless of ability.

Three County Star and Annie Questions are both flagged as fading in the finish and are being mapped further forward than their natural style — watch for both to drop out quickly from three fences out if the race develops into a stamina test.

races.name: Europe Hotel And Resort Handicap Steeplechase (Div II)

runners_data.name: The Rebel County
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid good-ground form (11/15 sim-going, 1W 2P) for G Ahern; Alan O'Sullivan takes the 5lb claim and 15 days since last run suggests freshness, but 168lbs and a wide draw in a big field makes traffic a serious concern.
runners_data.comment: Three top-four efforts in four starts before a blank last time, and quick to reappear just 15 days later over a trip he's already proven with. Still without a win through that sequence — the query on an otherwise solid profile.

runners_data.name: Huntsgrove
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who shows well on good ground (13/15, 1W 6P) for John Patrick Ryan, whose yard is in decent form (3/16 in 14 days); 49 days off and the step back from softer ground last time should suit.
runners_data.comment: Yet to feature in the frame across his last five starts and was pulled up 49 days ago, though he's already proven over today's trip and our figures rate him among the leading contenders. That stale form is the concern.

runners_data.name: Temptationinmilan
runners_data.note: Veteran 10-year-old hold-up horse with a modest record (0W 0P sim-going) and a string of mid-teen finishes; Ms A T O'Reilly's 7lb claim is a plus but the form figures of P450-7 give little confidence at this level.
runners_data.comment: A workmanlike sequence — no better than fourth in his last five — undersells him, with our figures rating him well clear of his official mark and a return to a trip he's already proven over. Fifty-seven days off the track is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Kilkee Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won his most recent start at 22f on soft, handled good ground before, and arrives for E McNamara 39 days fresh; the hood (b) and Mr J Dunne's 7lb claim are noteworthy, and this trip on good ground looks within range.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to end a mixed spell that also featured a fall and an unseated rider, and he's already proven over today's trip. Encouraging form on balance, though the jumping errors earlier in that sequence remain a concern.

runners_data.name: Stretchemout
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won at 21f on good ground and has placed twice at this trip; 15 days since last run and the tongue-tie plus cheekpieces suggest connections are live, though a P last time and 162lbs are mild negatives.
runners_data.comment: A win earlier in her sequence has given way to a downward curve — 4th, 7th, pulled up, then a finish outside the frame last time — though she's quick to reappear just 15 days later over a trip she's proven with.

runners_data.name: Parkgarve
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for Ian Donoghue (0/11 in 14 days is quiet) who has placed three times on good ground; 34 days since last run, 160lbs and a tongue-tie — no win in last six but keeps hitting the frame.
runners_data.comment: Modest recent form with only steady progress from 8th to 5th across his last three starts, and no better than that in the spell. Still without a win, he returns 34 days on from his latest run and needs more to trouble these.

runners_data.name: Schiehallion
runners_data.note: Prominent type who ran second at 24f on good ground two runs back (0W 3P sim-going); Dermot McLoughlin's yard is quiet (0/15 in 14 days) but the horse has sound jumping credentials and this trip suits.
runners_data.comment: A runner-up effort three starts back shows genuine ability, but it's bookended by two pulled-up runs and a fall further back, with his latest outing 34 days ago yielding only 5th. Already proven over today's trip, he's still without a win across this sequence.

runners_data.name: My Cullen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with mixed good-ground figures (6/14, 0W 1P) and a recent fall in form; Harry Sexton's 7lb claim helps the weight but the 91 OR and 52-day absence from competition make this a speculative interest.
runners_data.comment: A modest sequence — no finish better than sixth in his last five, including a fall — offers little to work with, and the stable has drawn a blank from 27 runners lately. Proven over today's trip, he returns 52 days off that.

runners_data.name: Ferdia
runners_data.note: In reality a hold-up horse for John Patrick Ryan — displaced into the midfield on the map because the rear is oversubscribed in this field; 34 days since last run, aged 10, and form figures of PP9-68 suggest he is just below the required level.
runners_data.comment: Vastly superior on our figures to his current official mark, suggesting untapped scope, and he's already proven over today's trip. But that gap has to be squared with a sorry run of results — 8th, 6th, 9th and two pulled-up efforts — the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Oogum Boogum
runners_data.note: Well-credentialled prominent racer with a win and six places on good ground (1W 6P) for David Budds; OR 84 is competitive and recent form of 3P-132 shows he is in a rich vein, making him one of the most naturally suited horses to the likely race shape.
runners_data.comment: A progressive sort, placed in each of his last three starts including a win, and he's already proven over today's trip. The one blip in that sequence was a pulled-up effort four starts back, and he returns 42 days on from his latest run.

runners_data.name: U Asking Me
runners_data.note: Prominent-style handicapper with decent good-ground experience (1W 4P) but a run of P3-7P0 dampens enthusiasm; 15 days between runs and 148lbs with the tongue-tie/cheekpieces combination suggest connections are testing options.
runners_data.comment: A third-placed effort four starts back is the highlight of a sequence that has since faded through 7th, a pulled-up run and an unplaced finish last time. He reappeared 15 days ago over a trip he's proven with, but the recent trend is the concern.

runners_data.name: Three Tribes
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse pushed into the midfield on the map due to field congestion, and also flagged as a fader in the finish; form of 80P1-P and modest sim-going figures (5/8) paint a difficult picture for a 9-year-old at this level.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up when last seen 57 days ago, continuing an erratic sequence that also featured a win two starts back sandwiched between two other pulled-up efforts. Our figures make him only par with his official mark, and there's little consistency to build a case on.

runners_data.name: Cullenwaine
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type who has placed four times on good ground (1W 3P) and ran twice in the last fortnight; OR 75 and the hood suggest value framing, and 3lb claimer Shane O'Callaghan adds interest.
runners_data.comment: A frequent frame-filler but winless across this sequence, with two runner-up efforts three and four starts back giving way to a 5th and 4th more recently. Only 16th of 18 on our figures, though he reappeared 15 days ago and is proven over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Robin Elite
runners_data.note: Holds-up but lacks the finish to capitalise — flagged as a fader and redistributed away from the rear; 0W 1P on good ground and a string of 0s and Ps in recent starts make this hard to recommend in an 18-runner field.
runners_data.comment: A miserable sequence — three pulled-up efforts and two finishes outside the frame from his last five starts — offers no sign of ability to work with. He returns 61 days after that, rated only modestly ahead of his official mark on our figures.

runners_data.name: The Border Boy
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer in nature but unable to secure that slot in this crowded field — mapped to midfield by necessity; Phillip Enright is a quality rider but OR 72 and form 638-04 are modest, and the horse's best trips have been shorter.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of the field on our figures, though the form itself isn't without redeeming features — a 3rd four starts back and a 4th last time out sandwich two weaker efforts. Proven over today's trip, he returns 48 days on from that latest run.

runners_data.name: Embrace The Day
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, likely to bowl along from the off for Gavin Cromwell; the fade flag and limited good-ground form (2/8 sim-going) are genuine concerns over 2m7f, but winning last time out and being the freshest pace influence gives the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to cap a sequence that had also featured two runs down the field, and he's proven over today's trip. But the stable has managed one winner from 45 in the past fortnight, and our figures rate him below his official mark.

runners_data.name: Watty Show
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type for Henry De Bromhead (4/35 T14 — stable is active) shown in midfield only because the rear is over-populated; fade flag attached, poor sim-going record (6/8), and form of 7P0-78 offers minimal encouragement.
runners_data.comment: A sequence with nothing better than 7th in five starts, including a pulled-up effort and a finish outside the frame, offers little encouragement. Our figures actually rate her below her official mark, and she's already proven over today's trip without ever threatening to feature there.

runners_data.name: Amburana
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Padraig Butler, shifted into midfield on the map as the rear is overcrowded; fade flag noted, only 6/9 on comparable going, and form of 043-70 leaves this looking like a participation entry rather than a winning chance.
runners_data.comment: A 3rd three starts back is as good as it gets in a modest sequence that has since faded through 7th and an unplaced run last time. Only 17th of 18 on our figures, she returns 50 days on with plenty to find.

races.paceDynamic: Embrace The Day is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Keith Donoghue aboard for Gavin Cromwell, will press on from the outset over this stiff 2m7f trip — but carries a fade flag and has limited recent good-ground form (2/8 sim-going), meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly searching. Behind the leader, Kilkee Bay, Parkgarve, Schiehallion, Oogum Boogum, U Asking Me and Cullenwaine are all genuine prominent types who will jostle for the chasing positions, creating a competitive but not frantic gallop that should nonetheless be sustained enough to stretch the field. The hold-up brigade — The Rebel County, Huntsgrove, Stretchemout and My Cullen — will settle toward the rear of a strung-out field, requiring a clear run and meaningful pace to peg back leaders over the final fences. This field contains more prominent types than positions available — The Border Boy, Ferdia and Watty Show are genuine front-to-midfield horses who are unlikely to secure their natural slots and will be squeezed into unfamiliar territory; of those available, Kilkee Bay and Oogum Boogum look best placed to actually hold prominent berths. The overall shape favours a prominent racer with stamina and sound jumping who can track Embrace The Day and take over in the straight, rather than a hold-up horse relying on a strong pace to close off.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Embrace The Day sets a honest but manageable gallop and a prominent tracker moves smoothly into contention from the third-last.
scenarios.body: Kilkee Bay or Oogum Boogum can sit just off the front-runner, conserve energy over the first circuit and deliver a decisive jump at the last two fences as Embrace The Day weakens; both carry course-confidence and good-ground form at this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Embrace The Day jumps fluently throughout and the field fails to mount a coordinated challenge, leaving the leader with enough in reserve at the last.
scenarios.body: The prominent pack cancels each other out in the chasing positions, the hold-up horses are never close enough to threaten, and Embrace The Day's superior OR of 100 and fresh-enough legs see it home; Cromwell's two wins from 45 runs in 14 days gives context but the horse won last time out and age (5) is an asset.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack burns more fuel than expected in the early exchanges and a gap opens up between the last two fences for a closer.
scenarios.body: The Rebel County or Huntsgrove, settled well off the pace, need a genuinely honest gallop to close ground and have the sim-going figures (11/15 and 13/15 respectively) to suggest they handle these conditions; however, an 18-runner field creates traffic risks that reduce the reliability of this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded field produces significant jumping errors, fallers or a chaotic early gallop that scrambles the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: An 18-runner steeplechase on good ground at Killarney is inherently unpredictable, and with several riders on claim allowances and horses out of their natural position (Ferdia, Watty Show, Three Tribes all racing away from their roles), a messy race could produce a surprise winner from the chasing pack.

watchPoints.text: Embrace The Day — watch the jumping quality early; if it makes a significant error in the first mile it will lose the lead it depends upon and the entire race shape collapses.

Kilkee Bay and Oogum Boogum — both prominent types bidding for the same chasing position behind the leader; if they crowd each other or one is checked, the likely winner of this shape could be knocked out of contention.
Ferdia and Watty Show — both true hold-up horses being carried into unfamiliar midfield territory by field size; watch whether they can settle or get competitive and use energy too early.

The Rebel County and Huntsgrove — the two most credentialled hold-up horses in the field; if there is any late pace collapse, watch whether Alan O'Sullivan or Brian Barry can find a gap in an 18-runner field from the back.

Three Tribes and Robin Elite — both flagged as natural hold-ups redistributed to midfield AND as faders; if either gets into a prominent position through early confusion, expect them to weaken after the third-last.
